briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Rides High on Sales Records as National Deals and Psychedelics Momentum Build
briefs.top: Michigan cements itself as the per-capita cannabis sales leader in the U.S. and crosses $17 billion all-time, even as the industry keeps fighting the 24% wholesale tax in court and at the ballot box. Nationally, Curaleaf's sweetened bid for Aurora Cannabis and Compass Pathways' march toward an FDA filing show capital and innovation still flowing despite a temporary pause in the DEA's rescheduling review.

local.text: Michigan tops the nation in per-capita weed sales — New 2026 analysis ranks Michigan first among recreational states on a per-resident basis, ahead of New Mexico, Montana and Massachusetts.
State market blows past $17 billion all-time — Combined medical and adult-use sales have now generated an estimated $2.66 billion in state excise and sales taxes since legalization.

GOP governor hopeful courts cannabis industry with tax-cut vow — Republican nominee John James has promised to repeal or sharply cut the 24% wholesale tax, and the state's top cannabis executives have rallied behind him.

Bad Axe voters set to end local dispensary ban — A citizen-initiated ballot measure this November would let up to two marijuana businesses open in the Thumb-region city for the first time since its 2019 prohibition.

Industry celebrates top brands at Zalympix even as tax fight grinds on — A fresh batch of Zalympix award winners landed the same week cannabis executives doubled down on political endorsements tied to repealing the 24% wholesale tax.

national.text: Curaleaf sweetens its bid to acquire Aurora Cannabis — The enhanced offer now implies $5 per Aurora share and would create a cannabis company operating across 17 countries with over $1.5 billion in trailing revenue.

Compass Pathways nears the finish line on psilocybin therapy — The company is still targeting a Q4 2026 FDA filing for COMP360, which could become the first classic psychedelic medicine ever approved in the U.S.

DEA rescheduling hits a procedural pause, not a reversal — A judge stayed the Schedule III hearing to weigh a new GAO report, but the pause doesn't touch the earlier order already protecting state-licensed medical marijuana businesses.

Vireo Growth becomes the nation's No. 2 dispensary network — Its acquisition of Cannabist assets across Colorado, Illinois, Massachusetts, New Jersey and West Virginia pushes the operator's footprint to 15 states.
Big Tobacco doubles down on cannabis as a growth bet — Organigram's largest shareholder, British American Tobacco, called cannabis a long-term opportunity under its 'Beyond Nicotine' roadmap to 2035.
